builder.representation: Closed layer prisms with between-plane numerical guard; no whole-model Boolean or STL roundtrip
limitations: Between-plane geometry is specialized to this layer schedule; do not rotate, scale, or change layer heights.
Wall displacement and seam behavior require separate slicing comparison.
Source contours are regularized on the reported numerical binary grid before the simplification reference; sub-grid cracks can close.
NOWEAVE display colors are preserved when uniform and known; source extruder numbers are provenance only and require printer mapping.
Copied source meshes are not repaired or independently certified as float32-safe closed solids.
Single-layer complexity is budget-limited; oversized sections fail instead of using legacy memory-heavy fallback.

numerical_policy.boundary_certificate_precision: Float64 boundary copies with fixed-precision metadata cleared before conservative buffering; coordinates unchanged.
numerical_policy.regularization: Both independently decoded artifacts use the common binary-grid contour policy before comparison.
numerical_policy.complete_vertical_quad_policy: Recovered rectangle-edge vertices bypass intermediate intersection rounding; exactly-on-lattice sections receive pointwise precision metadata without topology normalization. A single already-certified section per material bypasses redundant fixed-precision union; generic and multiple-input sections retain regularization and union.

passthrough.method: Indexed float64 geometry plus source color/extruder provenance; transforms and reflected winding included. Legacy nine-decimal rounding is used only when the candidate predates explicit coordinate encoding.

final_serialized_audit.method: Independent serialized-artifact re-slicing; certified two-way boundary-buffer containment plus component/hole and overlap topology checks on every fixed-height slicing plane.
limitations: Shares the slicing kernel with the exporter; not a separate kernel proof.
Comparison is to numerically regularized source contours; grids and cleanup are disclosed above.
Wall centerlines, extrusion widths, seams, and supports require downstream slicer/G-code validation.
Does not certify full-mesh manifold topology away from slicing planes.

fallback_forensics.scope: Read-only geometry investigation: no backend or 3MF changes, no full-model mesh materialized. Disk-backed source sections reconstructed independently.

sample.method: 80 evenly spaced fallback layers ordered by height, plus 12 evenly spaced accepted controls

interpretation: Most sampled rejections begin at combined-union or color-overlap guards, after every individual material has stayed within the 0.02mm bound and retained its own signature. This identifies contacts/seams between materials as the main sampled cause.

Many disappearing or appearing features are long slits or overlap slivers with extremely small area and width. Boundary Hausdorff distance can then be millimeters because a boundary appears/disappears far from the surviving boundary, even while each material contour moves under 0.015mm.

A smaller group changes single-material connectivity, hole count, or narrow bays. These include a roughly 0.00587mm-width hole and a roughly 0.00236mm-width filled bay; rejection is not exclusively machine-roundoff-sized features.
The final binary-grid guard correctly catches additional failures that passed the initial candidate guard. All 12 sampled export-grid cases first failed a material guard.

The reported candidates were rejected: the delivered weave retained the original reference geometry for these layers. This forensic analysis does not establish whether a slicer would print the tiny seams; actual wall-toolpath comparison is needed.
Width values use 2*area/perimeter as a scale proxy, not a certified minimum feature width. Counts of changed features may include the same local feature in more than one material/union/overlap guard.

examples.finding: Export-grid snap fills a narrow bay: area 0.005283mm2, bbox diagonal 2.2395mm, width proxy 0.002359mm; component/hole counts unchanged but boundary displacement becomes 1.1155mm.

All material boundaries stay within 0.01495mm, but a thin fissure appears on the magenta/yellow join. New union-boundary point is 0.19205mm from old union boundary while lying on both old material boundaries. Local removed area 4.0563e-7mm2; width proxy 1.9807e-6mm.

Union hole count changes 1 to 0; filled long slit area 1.5477e-5mm2, bbox diagonal 1.6227mm, width proxy 9.538e-6mm. Another join fissure contributes the 0.23665mm union-boundary discrepancy. All material boundaries stay within 0.01497mm.
Yellow changes from 15 components/1 hole to 14 components/2 holes even though all material boundary displacements remain below 0.01498mm: a topology-only per-material rejection.

One of two magenta/yellow overlap components disappears: area 5.6591e-6mm2, bbox diagonal 0.765945mm, width proxy 7.3883e-6mm. Overlap Hausdorff becomes 2.0136mm while material boundaries remain under 0.01495mm.

Magenta loses a long narrow hole: area 0.0173571mm2, bbox diagonal 2.9554mm, width proxy 0.0058726mm. This is a larger narrow feature than the numerical seam examples, with 1.9334mm boundary discrepancy if accepted.

unchanged_source_after_auditor_fix.method: One layer at a time; cache original slice_part outputs and compare prior unconditional union with current layer_regions, only for sections entering the newly added branch. All other code paths are identical.
